holidays.name: National Yo-Yo Day
holidays.description: A day to dust off your favorite string-and-spool toy and try a Walk the Dog, Around the World, or Rock the Baby. Beginners are welcome to tangle themselves up in the fun.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It celebrates one of the world's longest-lived toys, which was popularized in America in the late 1920s.
holidays.funFact: Filipino-American entrepreneur Pedro Flores began mass-producing yo-yos in California in the 1920s. Donald Duncan later bought his company and turned the toy into a national craze.

holidays.name: Drive-In Movie Day
holidays.description: A salute to watching films from the comfort of your car, with snacks in the back seat and a big screen under the stars. Pack blankets, popcorn, and a good speaker, and enjoy a double feature.
holidays.origin: The date marks the anniversary of the first U.S. drive-in theater, which opened in Camden, New Jersey, on June 6, 1933. Richard Hollingshead created it.
holidays.funFact: Hollingshead reportedly tested his idea by mounting a projector on his car hood and hanging a screen in his driveway. He wanted to make movies comfortable for people who didn't fit well in theater seats.

holidays.name: National Applesauce Cake Day
holidays.description: A day for a moist, spiced, comforting cake made with applesauce. Bake one for dessert, or just have a slice with your coffee.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It honors a homey cake that has long been a staple of American baking.
holidays.funFact: Applesauce cakes were popular in thrifty kitchens in the early 20th century. Applesauce stood in for scarce butter, eggs, and sugar, and it kept the cake moist for days.
